mainTopic: Rose oil on שבת and רב's ruling like רבי שמעון "but not for his reason"; the close of פרק שמונה שרצים; and the opening משניות and גמרא on which knots are חייב, פטור, or permitted on שבת.
overview: This עמוד opens by finishing the question of whether רב really rules like רבי שמעון about smearing rose oil on שבת. The barrel-tap case proves nothing, because it is a פסיק רישיה, where even רבי שמעון forbids. רבא then explains that רב follows רבי שמעון's ruling but not his reason. For רב, rose oil is permitted only where it is common, and in his area it was. The פרק שמונה שרצים ends with its הדרן, and a new פרק on knots begins. The משנה says permanent knots, like the camel drivers' and sailors' knots, make one חייב, while רבי מאיר exempts any knot that can be untied with one hand. The גמרא identifies these knots as the ones that hold the rings themselves in place. It leaves unresolved (תיקו) how רבי מאיר would rule on a bow. A second משנה lists everyday knots, and the גמרא resolves a contradiction in its wording by showing that it describes two kinds of non-liable knots. The details continue on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רב forbids tightly stuffing a barrel tap on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The end of a challenge: רב himself said it is forbidden to stuff a barrel tap tightly on יום טוב. That sounds like he does not hold like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is forbidden to stuff it tightly on יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question that began on the previous עמוד. רב said one may not tightly stuff a rag into a barrel's tap on יום טוב, because liquid will be squeezed out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון usually permits a דבר שאין מתכוין, an act where the forbidden result is not intended. If רב forbids stuffing the tap even though no one intends to squeeze, he seems to hold like רבי יהודה. That clashes with his ruling like רבי שמעון about rose oil.

keyTerms.meaning: an act where the forbidden result is not intended

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new ruling. It is the punchline of a challenge that started on the previous עמוד, against רב's ruling like רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: It is forbidden to insert it tightly on a Festival!
phrases.notes: Pressing the cloth in tightly will squeeze out liquid (סחיטה).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge begun on the previous עמוד.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון regarding rose oil.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב forbids an unintended forbidden result (squeezing), which is רבי יהודה's view, not רבי שמעון's.

steps.title: Even רבי שמעון agrees when the result is certain
steps.stepSummary: Stuffing the tap is a פסיק רישיה, where the forbidden result is unavoidable. רבי שמעון agrees that such a case is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: In that case even רבי שמעון agrees. אביי and רבא both said: רבי שמעון agrees in a case of "cut off its head and won't it die?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the barrel case proves nothing. In that case even רבי שמעון would forbid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון permits an unintended result only when it might not happen. If the result is certain, like cutting off a head and expecting it not to die, he forbids. Tightly stuffing a wet rag will certainly squeeze liquid, so רב's ruling there fits רבי שמעון too.

keyTerms.meaning: "Cut off its head and won't it die?": a forbidden result that is unavoidable

steps.whyThisMatters: פסיק רישיה is a basic rule across all of הלכות שבת. Even those who permit an unintended act forbid it when the forbidden result is certain.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי שמעון permits every unintended act. His leniency stops at פסיק רישיה.

phrases.english: In that case even Rabbi Shimon agrees.
For Abaye and Rava both said:
Rabbi Shimon agrees
in a case of "cut off its head and won't it die?"
phrases.notes: Of course it will die! It's a picture of a result that's bound to happen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the barrel case is a פסיק רישיה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's barrel ruling shows he rejects רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The barrel ruling fits רבי שמעון, because the squeezing is inevitable.

steps.title: An explicit tradition that רב rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings two chains of tradition. In both, רב rules like רבי יהודה and שמואל rules like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. And רב חנן בר אמי said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. And רב חייא בר אבין taught it without the transmitters' names: רב said the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, and שמואל said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks again, now with a direct statement. רב explicitly rules like רבי יהודה against רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 only removed one indirect proof. Here a clear tradition says רב follows רבי יהודה in his disputes with רבי שמעון. A second version, taught without the middle names, gives the same result. So how could רב rule like רבי שמעון about rose oil?

keyTerms.meaning: without the men, i.e., without the names of the transmitters

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi say that Rav said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חָנָן בַּר אַמֵּי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: and Rav Ḥanan bar Ami said that Shmuel said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין מַתְנֵי לַהּ בְּלָא גַבְרֵי,
phrases.english: And Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin taught it without the names of the men in between:
Rav said: The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
and Shmuel said: The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 2 deflected the indirect proof, a stronger, direct challenge is raised.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling like רבי שמעון regarding rose oil.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit tradition, reported in two versions (with and without the names of the transmitters), records רב ruling like רבי יהודה, against רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבא: like רבי שמעון, but not for his reason
steps.stepSummary: רבא, together with רבי חייא בר אבין ("the lion of the group"), explains that רב follows רבי שמעון's result but not his reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: I and the lion of the group explained it. And who is that? רבי חייא בר אבין. The הלכה follows רבי שמעון, but not for his reason.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves the contradiction. רב agrees with רבי שמעון's bottom line about rose oil, but for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב does not accept רבי שמעון's reasoning, he is not really siding with him against רבי יהודה. He only reaches the same practical result here through his own logic. The next steps explain what that different reasoning is.

keyTerms.meaning: the lion of the group, a title of honor

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
I and the lion of the group explained it:
And who is he? Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin:
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon, but not for his reason.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא אֲנִי וַאֲרִי שֶׁבַּחֲבוּרָה תַּרְגֵּימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's ruling on rose oil means he follows רבי שמעון's approach.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב shares רבי שמעון's result here only, not his reasoning, so it does not conflict with his general ruling like רבי יהודה.

steps.title: What does 'not for his reason' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact meaning of רבא's phrase.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by "the הלכה follows רבי שמעון, but not for his reason"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבא's phrase. It is setting up two possible explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "not for his reason" is not enough. We need to know which reason רב rejects and what he says instead.

phrases.english: What is meant by "the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon, but not for his reason"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְלָאו מִטַּעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the answer given in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which reason of רבי שמעון רב rejects, and what רב's own reason is.

steps.title: First suggestion: רב thinks rose oil does not heal
steps.stepSummary: A first try: רבי שמעון holds rose oil heals but permits it anyway, while רב permits it because he thinks it does not heal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון in that it is permitted, but not for his reason, because רבי שמעון holds it heals and רב holds it does not heal...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first explanation, introduced with אילימא ("if you say"). Expect it to be rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, רב permits rose oil because it is not medicine at all, so the ban on healing on שבת does not apply. רבי שמעון, by contrast, admits it heals but still permits it. Same result, different reason.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say: introduces a suggestion that will be rejected

phrases.english: If you say: the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon, who permits it,
but not for his reason,
since Rabbi Shimon holds that it heals,
and Rav holds that it does not heal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב permits rose oil because he holds it has no healing effect.

steps.title: The משנה shows rose oil does heal
steps.stepSummary: The first suggestion is rejected. The משנה says princes put rose oil on their wounds, which shows it heals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רב really hold it does not heal? But since it is taught, "Princes smear rose oil on their wounds," we can infer that it heals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first suggestion from the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would princes put rose oil on wounds unless it heals? Since the משנה assumes it is medicinal, רב cannot simply say it doesn't heal. The first explanation falls.

phrases.english: And does Rav hold that it does not heal?
But from the fact that it is taught:
"Princes smear on their wounds
rose oil,"
by inference, it heals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the explanation given in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב holds rose oil does not heal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה describes rose oil being used on wounds, which shows it is medicinal.

steps.title: Final explanation: it depends on whether rose oil is common
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון permits rose oil even where it is rare. רב permits it only where it is common, and in רב's area it was common.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון in that it is permitted, but not for his reason. רבי שמעון holds that even if it is not common, it is permitted. רב holds that if it is common, yes, and if it is not common, no. And in רב's place, rose oil was common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning of "not for his reason." For רב, the key factor is whether rose oil is commonly used where you live.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where rose oil is rare and expensive, anyone who smears it is clearly doing it as medicine, so רב forbids it. Where it is common, people use it as ordinary oil, so it does not look like healing. רבי שמעון permits it everywhere. רב permitted it only because rose oil was common in his area.
steps.whatToRemember: "הלכה כרבי שמעון ולאו מטעמיה" means this: רב agrees rose oil may be used on שבת, but only where it is common. Rare rose oil looks like medicine and is forbidden. רב's ruling reflected his own locale.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key idea in the laws of healing on שבת. What matters is whether the act looks like medicine, and that can depend on local custom.

phrases.english: Rather: the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon, who permits it,
but not for his reason,
since Rabbi Shimon holds:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא שְׁכִיחַ, שְׁרֵי.
phrases.english: even though it is not common, it is permitted.
And Rav holds: if it is common, yes,
and if it is not common, no.
And in Rav's place, rose oil was common.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּשָׁרֵי וְלָאו מִטַּעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation rejected in step 7 with the correct one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the reason: the difference is about how common rose oil is, not whether it heals.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב permits rose oil because he thinks it is not medicine.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב admits rose oil heals, but permits it only where it is common, because there smearing it does not look like healing.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק שמונה שרצים
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק שמונה שרצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, שמונה שרצים.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line marking the end of the chapter שמונה שרצים. No new argument is made here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן expresses the hope to return and learn the chapter again. The next chapter begins after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: we will return to you: the formula for finishing a chapter
"Eight creeping creatures": the name of the chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, Shemonah Sheratzim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter שמונה שרצים is complete.

steps.title: New chapter: the knots that make you liable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens the new פרק. The camel driver's knot and the sailor's knot make a person חייב on שבת, and untying them makes him חייב too.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These are the knots you are liable for: the camel drivers' knot and the sailors' knot. Just as he is liable for tying them, he is liable for untying them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins the new פרק. It names the two main examples of knots that break שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying (קושר) and untying (מתיר) are both among the 39 מלאכות. The משנה gives two model knots and says both actions apply to them equally. The גמרא will soon ask what exactly these two knots are.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable, meaning a real Torah violation (one who does it by mistake brings a קרבן חטאת)

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these are the knots that one is liable for:
the camel drivers' knot and the sailors' knot,
and just as he is liable for tying them,
so too he is liable for untying them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tying or untying a camel driver's knot or a sailor's knot makes one חייב on שבת.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: a one-hand knot is not liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says that any knot you can untie with one hand does not make you חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: Any knot that one can untie with one of his hands, one is not liable for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives a general rule for telling which knots count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's test is whether the knot is easy to undo with one hand. If it is, it does not count as a real knot for חיוב. The גמרא will later ask what the reason behind this test really is.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
any knot that he can untie
with one of his hands,
one is not liable for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל קֶשֶׁר שֶׁהוּא יָכוֹל לְהַתִּירוֹ בְּאַחַת מִיָּדָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second opinion with a general rule to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A knot that can be untied with one hand does not make one חייב.

steps.title: Which knots are the camel and sailor knots?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the camel drivers' knot and the sailors' knot are.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What are the camel drivers' knot and the sailors' knot?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks us to identify the two knots named in the משנה. It is setting up the attempted answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Camel drivers and sailors tie many different knots. To know the הלכה, we need to know which one the משנה means.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the camel drivers' knot
and the sailors' knot?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define the terms in step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific knots the משנה means

steps.title: First guess: the knots tied to the rings
steps.stepSummary: The first suggestion is the knot that ties a rope to the camel's nose ring and the knot that ties a rope to the ship's ring.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is the knot they tie onto the nose ring, and the knot they tie onto the ship's ring...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first answer. The word אילימא ("if you say") signals that this answer is about to be rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the משנה means the rope a driver ties to the camel's nose ring to lead it, and the rope sailors tie to the ring on the ship to dock it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that will be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say: the knot that they tie onto the nose ring,
and the knot that they tie onto the ship's ring,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A first attempted answer to the question in step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ropes tied onto the nose ring and onto the ship's ring

steps.title: Rejected: those knots are not permanent
steps.stepSummary: The guess is rejected. Those knots are untied all the time, so they are not a קשר של קיימא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a knot that is not permanent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first guess.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A knot only makes a person חייב if it is meant to last (של קיימא). A rope tied to lead a camel or dock a ship is untied regularly, so it cannot be the knot the משנה calls חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent knot, one meant to last

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the basic rule of the whole פרק: only a lasting knot is a Torah-level violation.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי קֶשֶׁר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁל קַיָּימָא הוּא!
phrases.english: This is a knot that is not permanent!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי קֶשֶׁר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁל קַיָּימָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 13
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Those knots are temporary, and only a permanent knot makes one חייב

steps.title: Correct answer: the knots that hold the rings themselves
steps.stepSummary: The knots meant are the ones that fasten the nose ring itself onto the camel and the ring itself onto the ship. These knots stay tied.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is the knot of the nose ring itself, and of the ship's ring itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. אלא ("rather") marks the replacement for the rejected guess.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ring is fastened to the camel or to the ship with a knot that is never untied. That makes it permanent, so it fits the rule of קשר של קיימא.
steps.whatToRemember: The camel drivers' knot and the sailors' knot are the knots that hold the rings in place. They are permanent knots, and that is why they make a person חייב.

phrases.english: Rather: the knot of the nose ring itself,
and that of the ship's ring itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the guess that was rejected in step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The permanent knots that attach the rings themselves

steps.title: רב אחדבוי asks about a bow according to רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי מאיר. רב אחדבוי then asks how רבי מאיר would rule on a bow (עניבה).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: any knot, etc. רב אחדבוי, brother of מר אחא, asked: What is the law of a bow according to רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to רבי מאיר's opinion and raises a question about it. It is setting up the two sides of the question that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bow can be pulled open with one hand, but it can also be pulled very tight. So it is unclear which side of רבי מאיר's rule it falls on.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר כׇּל קֶשֶׁר כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: any knot, etc.

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי רַב אַחָדְבוּי אַחוּי דְּמָר אַחָא:
phrases.english: Rav Achadvoy, brother of Mar Acha, asked:
A bow, according to Rabbi Meir, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב אַחָדְבוּי אַחוּי דְּמָר אַחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the camel and sailor knots to רבי מאיר's rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי מאיר would hold a person חייב for tying a bow

steps.title: The two sides: easy to untie, or not tight?
steps.stepSummary: Is רבי מאיר's reason that the knot can be untied with one hand, which fits a bow? Or is it that such knots are not tight, while a bow is tight?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is רבי מאיר's reason that one can untie it with one hand, and this too can be untied? Or perhaps רבי מאיר's reason is that it is not tight, and this one is tight?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the two possible reasons behind רבי מאיר's rule. Each reason gives a different answer for a bow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the test is ease of untying, so a bow is fine. Side two: one-hand untying is only a sign that the knot is loose, and a bow can be tight, so it would be חייב.

phrases.english: Is Rabbi Meir's reason because one can
untie it with one of his hands,
and this too he can untie?
Or perhaps Rabbi Meir's reason is
because it is not tight,
and this one is tight.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר מִשּׁוּם דְּיָכוֹל לְהַתִּירוֹ בְּאַחַת מִיָּדָיו הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the question in step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי מאיר's test is ease of untying or looseness

steps.title: The question stays open
steps.stepSummary: The question is left unresolved (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source decides between the two reasons. So the law of a bow according to רבי מאיר stays undecided.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand (the question remains unresolved)

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from steps 16 and 17
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a bow is חייב according to רבי מאיר remains unresolved.

steps.title: Second משנה: everyday knots that are not liable
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists knots that are not חייב like the camel and sailor knots: a woman's robe opening, hairnet strings, belt laces, shoe and sandal straps, wine and oil skins, and a cloth over a pot of meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There are knots one is not liable for like the camel drivers' knot and the sailors' knot. A woman may tie the opening of her robe, the strings of her hairnet, and those of her belt, shoe and sandal straps, wine and oil skins, and a pot of meat.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives a list of common knots that are not treated like the חייב knots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All of these knots are tied and untied regularly, so none of them is permanent. The opening line, "not liable like the camel knot," suggests a lighter rabbinic issue. The rest of the list, however, says "a woman may tie," which sounds fully permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A wide belt tied with laces

steps.confusionAlert: "Not liable" usually means forbidden by the חכמים but not by the Torah. Here, though, the list says these knots may be tied outright. The גמרא deals with exactly this tension in steps 21–22.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ יֵשׁ לְךָ קְשָׁרִין שֶׁאֵין חַיָּיבִין עֲלֵיהֶן
phrases.english: MISHNA: You have knots that one is not liable for
as for the camel drivers' knot and the sailors' knot:
a woman may tie the opening of her robe,
and the strings of a hairnet, and those of a belt,
and the straps of a shoe and a sandal,
and skins of wine and oil,
and a pot of meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ יֵשׁ לְךָ קְשָׁרִין שֶׁאֵין חַיָּיבִין עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה that contrasts with the חייב knots of step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Common temporary knots, such as clothing ties, shoe straps, and flask ties, may be tied and are not like the חייב knots.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: a rope in front of an animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds that one may tie a rope in front of an animal to keep it from leaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: One may tie in front of an animal so that it will not go out.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא adds one more case to the list of allowed knots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rope tied across a doorway to keep an animal in is taken down regularly. That makes it a temporary knot, just like the items on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: So that it will not go out

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
one may tie in front of an animal
so that it will not go out.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: קוֹשְׁרִין לִפְנֵי הַבְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more allowed case to the list in step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may tie a rope in front of an animal to keep it from leaving.

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that 'not חייב' implies an איסור still exists, yet the משנה then lists a woman tying her robe, which sounds permitted even לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This משנה contradicts itself! You said, 'There are knots one is not liable for, like the camel drivers' knot and the sailors' knot.' That means there is no liability, but there is still a prohibition. Then it teaches, 'A woman may tie the opening of her robe,' which means it is allowed even from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by pointing out that its opening line and its examples do not seem to match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'אין חייבין' normally means פטור אבל אסור: no punishment, but still forbidden. But the example 'קושרת אשה' uses language of permission, meaning מותר לכתחילה. So the opening and the list seem to describe two different levels of law.

keyTerms.meaning: This statement itself is difficult (it contradicts itself)
Liability (being חייב a punishment or a חטאת)
A prohibition (forbidden, even if there is no liability)
From the outset; allowed to do in the first place
The neck opening of her robe

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'אין חייבין' means 'permitted.' In the language of the משנה it usually means 'exempt from punishment but still forbidden.' That is exactly why the גמרא sees a contradiction.

phrases.english: Gemara
This itself is difficult:
You said there are knots
for which one is not liable
like the camel drivers' knot and the sailors' knot
It is liability that there is not,
but a prohibition there is,
and then it teaches:
A woman may tie the opening of her robe
which means even from the outset!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה quoted in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opening line of the משנה ('יש קשרין שאין חייבין עליהן') compared with its examples ('קושרת אשה').
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'אין חייבין' implies אסור, while 'קושרת' implies מותר לכתחילה. Both cannot describe the same knots.

steps.title: Rereading the משנה: two kinds of non-liable knots
steps.stepSummary: Using הכי קאמר, the גמרא explains that the משנה's opening refers to one group of knots: not liable like the camel and sailor knots, but still forbidden. It then asks which knots those are. The list starting 'קושרת אשה' is a separate, fully permitted group.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: There are knots that one is not liable for, the way one is liable for the camel drivers' knot and the sailors' knot. And which knots are these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by reading the משנה as describing two separate groups of knots. It then asks 'which are they,' setting up the identification of the first group, which continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening line is read as its own category: some knots are not חייב the way camel and sailor knots are, but they are still forbidden (פטור אבל אסור). The list beginning 'קושרת אשה' is a different category, knots that are מותר לכתחילה. Once the two clauses describe different knots, the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a rereading of the text)
Camel drivers' knot (a permanent knot that one is חייב for)
And which are they? (introduces a list)

steps.whatToRemember: Through הכי קאמר, the משנה is read as describing two groups. Some knots are exempt but forbidden. The listed everyday knots (robe opening, hairnet, belt, shoes, skins, pot cover) are fully permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up three levels of knots: חייב (permanent knots like camel and sailor knots), exempt but forbidden, and fully permitted (the everyday knots in the list).

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
There are knots for which one is not liable
as one is liable for the camel drivers' knot and the sailors' knot.
phrases.notes: These knots don't make you liable the way camel drivers' and sailors' knots do, but they're still forbidden.

phrases.english: And which are they?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is about to name this first group, and the answer continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the internal contradiction raised in Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The opening line and the list describe the same knots, so they must be either forbidden or permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The opening line names knots that carry no liability, unlike camel and sailor knots, but are still forbidden. The knots listed from 'קושרת אשה' are a separate group that is fully permitted.
